topics.definition: A deadlock is a situation where two or more processes wait indefinitely for resources held by each other.
topics.syntax: P1 waits for P2, P2 waits for P1
topics.example: Two processes waiting for each other's lock
tips: No process can continue until the deadlock is resolved.

topics.definition: Deadlock occurs when Mutual Exclusion, Hold and Wait, No Preemption and Circular Wait exist together.
tips: Breaking any one condition can prevent deadlock.

topics.definition: A graph used to represent processes, resources and their allocations.
Prevention ensures at least one necessary condition never occurs.
Avoidance allocates resources only if the system remains in a safe state.
tips: Requires advance knowledge of resource needs.

topics.definition: Detection identifies whether a deadlock has already occurred.
tips: Used when prevention is not implemented.

topics.definition: Recovery removes deadlocks by terminating processes or preempting resources.
Design systems to minimize deadlocks and monitor resource allocation.
tips: Acquire resources in a fixed order.
